fullPassage: Darwin understood that since inheritance is conservative, it is in the nature of organisms to look like their parents. But variation can also be inherited. That was the crucial insight. While most differences between parents and offspring are too small to notice, over long periods of time small changes add up. Darwin was able to grasp this because he worked with animal breeders and plant growers who understood the process well. Through selective breeding, they reshaped species to their liking. Resistance to change is the expected condition, but over vast scales of time, variation accumulates. Darwin envisioned that as change builds, new species can arise out of old ones, like a tree branching into increasingly different limbs. At the heart of this vision was the idea that, given enough time, the variations that exist within a species can expand beyond the original boundaries of that species, producing entirely new forms of life. This concept of gradual transformation was difficult for many to accept, because it suggested that all living things are connected through a shared ancestry.

questions.passage: Darwin understood that since inheritance is conservative, it is in the nature of organisms to look like their parents. But variation can also be inherited. That was the crucial insight. While most differences between parents and offspring are too small to notice, over long periods of time small changes add up. Darwin was able to grasp this because he worked with animal breeders and plant growers who understood the process well. Through selective breeding, they reshaped species to their liking. Resistance to change is the expected condition, but over vast scales of time, variation accumulates. Darwin envisioned that as change builds, new species can arise out of old ones, <u>like a tree branching into increasingly different limbs</u>. At the heart of this vision was the idea that, given enough time, the variations that exist within a species can expand beyond the original boundaries of that species, producing entirely new forms of life. This concept of gradual transformation was difficult for many to accept, because it suggested that all living things are connected through a shared ancestry.
